newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia sees 1997 inflation remaining steady.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia sees 1997 inflation remaining steady.

text.p: The Slovenian Ministry of Economic Affairs said on Monday that inflation should not rise this year despite expected price increases in electricity, petrol and telephone calls.

"We can not expect similar processes here as in some of our neighbouring countries as Hungary, where after two years of falling inflation it began rising again. But I cannot say what the exact inflation rate will be," Davor Valentincic, state secretary of trade at the Economic Affairs Ministry told a news conference.
He said the state would keep prices of medicine, petrol, electricity and telephone calls under control.

"Preventive measures of the state and especially, this ministry will be necesary also in the future in order to approach the European inflatory standards of some five or six percent," Janko Dezelak, Minister of Economic Affairs said.

Currently, electricity prices are about 20-percent lower than the EU average, petrol prices are 35 percent below the average and prices of domestic phone calls are six times lower than the EU average.
Slovenian inflation in 1996 rose to 8.8 percent from 8.6 percent in 1995, and economists have predicted steady prices in 1997.
